Figure 3:Relationship between cDFS and the auxiliary fidelity scores — Shape score (left) and Trend score (right) — across all three datasets pooled.
HorizonL=32L=32.
Higher is better on both axes.
The figure shows that high Shape and Trend scores do not, by themselves, imply a high cDFS: many baselines achieve competitive Shape or Trend values while collapsing along the cDFS axis, suggesting that cDFS is a more holistic criterion.

Higher is better on both axes.
Across all three views, TMS grows consistently with each matched submetric.
